stem: The national highway network project connecting India's four major metropolitan cities — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata — via a quadrilateral of high-speed roads, launched in 2001, is known as the:
explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata via the largest highway project in India at the time of its launch — distinct from the separately-built North-South/East-West Corridor (connecting extreme points of India) or newer projects like Bharatmala (comprehensive highway development) and Sagarmala (port-led development).
